Return one JSON object only, without Markdown.
Use {"status":"UNSUPPORTED","reason":"..."} if outside the finite language.
Otherwise use {"status":"ANSWER","calls":[selection],"combine":{"op":"single"}}.
A selection is {"nodes":[{"id":"n","label":"SCHEMA_LABEL"}],"edges":[],
"where":[],"returns":[{"field":"n.name","alias":"name"}]}.
Each calls item is directly this selection object; do not wrap it in a
"selection" or "query" field. No text before/after the JSON.
Up to4 nodes and3 connected directed edges; edges have id,source,target,label.
The first node is the required root. Mandatory edges form one Cypher MATCH:
distinct edge variables cannot reuse the same graph relationship.
At most one edge may have optional:true. It must attach to the required
pattern and may introduce a nullable neighbor. Use this when requested groups
must be preserved even when they have zero matching neighbors. Count a nullable
neighbor eid (or edge rid), not count(*) or a required root, to obtain zero.
An optional expansion after an anchor filter can count ALL neighbors, including
the anchor relationship; this is a separate Cypher matching stage.
All labels/properties and edge directions must match schema. Available node
metadata properties: eid,name,aliases,description. Edge metadata: rid.
where is an AND list of {field:"n.property",op:"eq",value:literal}; supported
ops eq,ne,lt,le,gt,ge,in,contains,starts_with,ends_with,is_null,not_null.
Each predicate may add negate:true, applying Cypher NOT with three-valued
NULL semantics. NOT unknown remains unknown and is rejected by WHERE.
where predicates apply globally after the optional match. A condition on the
nullable neighbor can therefore remove zero groups. Filtered optional counts
that require conditions inside the optional pattern are outside this version.
Set difference removes known positive entity sets; it is not automatically
equivalent to negating a nullable property predicate.
Use other_field instead of value for same-type property comparisons.
returns items have field and alias; optional agg=count|sum|avg|min|max|collect,
optional distinct boolean for aggregation. count may use field "*" or node ID.
Grouping is otherwise implicit from non-aggregate returns. To group per ENTITY,
add group_by:["n.eid"] (or the appropriate root eid); equal display names are
not guaranteed to be one entity. For grouping by a property value use that
property as a grouping key. Returned non-aggregate properties must be determined
by the keys. A filter-anchor neighbor and a neighbor to be counted may need
separate variables; do not count only the restricted anchor when all related
entities are requested.
Selection optional distinct boolean, order_by:[{column:alias,direction:"ASC"}],
limit:positive integer ONLY when explicitly requested; never add a default LIMIT.
For union/intersection/difference of ENTITY SETS use exactly2 selections. Each
must return the same columns, include projected n.eid as alias "id", and only
properties of that same answer entity. No input aggregation, order or limit.
combine is {op:"union"|"intersection"|"difference",key:"id",output:"count",
alias:"count"}, or output:"rows",columns:[requested output aliases].
This finite version does not support multiple optional edges, subqueries, arbitrary
expressions, regex, variable-length paths, arithmetic, HAVING, multi-stage
aggregation, joins of service summaries, or semantic relations absent in schema.
Do not replace an unsupported condition with an easier question.

Explicit compiler contract (v3; use these exact JSON positions): Every property reference is variable.property, using a node or edge id declared in the selection and a property declared for that binding. This applies to where.field and where.other_field; bare property names are not valid. For a distinct projection without aggregation, use selection-level distinct:true. A returns item may contain distinct only when that same item contains agg; even distinct:false is invalid on a non-aggregate returns item. For distinct counting use {field:<valid field>,alias:<output>,agg:"count",distinct:true}; COUNT DISTINCT * is not supported. Use group_by only when the selection has an aggregate, with one to four unique grouping keys. Every non-aggregate projection must be determined by those keys. order_by.column names a returned alias and direction is ASC or DESC. Do not emit an implicit limit. No more than one optional edge is supported; the required pattern must connect to the first/root node. Unsupported syntax must produce UNSUPPORTED; do not change the question or guess a property.
In this profile, returns.field and group_by use qualified properties. Only agg:"count" additionally permits field:"*" or a declared node variable; bare entities are not ordinary projections. Two-call composition requires a required, non-null answer-entity identity projected under the shared key alias, aligned columns and payload from that same entity type. Inputs must be unaggregated, unordered and unlimited. Use the supplied entity eid as the composition identity, e.g. n.eid. 
Syntax examples only: assume an illustrative ExampleEntity label with string key declared as identity_property; CypherBench also supplies eid. These are not task schema declarations. Replace the illustrative label and property with the actual public schema. The duplicated union inputs below show only the two-call structure, not a recommended plan for any task.

distinct_count: {"status":"ANSWER","calls":[{"nodes":[{"id":"n","label":"ExampleEntity"}],"edges":[],"where":[],"returns":[{"field":"n.eid","alias":"total","agg":"count","distinct":true}]}],"combine":{"op":"single"}}
entity_set: {"status":"ANSWER","calls":[{"nodes":[{"id":"n","label":"ExampleEntity"}],"edges":[],"where":[],"returns":[{"field":"n.eid","alias":"id"}]},{"nodes":[{"id":"n","label":"ExampleEntity"}],"edges":[],"where":[],"returns":[{"field":"n.eid","alias":"id"}]}],"combine":{"op":"union","key":"id","output":"count","alias":"total"}}

The engine is pinned native TuGraph 4.5.2, not Neo4j.
Only actual schema properties exist; entity identity is identity_property.
Do not assume eid, rid, aliases, name or description unless actually declared.
Use actual simple schema identifiers; quoted label spelling was not equivalent
in independent checks. Use explicit variable lists in WITH, not WITH *.
Separate consecutive MATCH/OPTIONAL stages using explicit WITH bindings.
Global post-OPTIONAL predicates require a subsequent explicit WITH stage;
carry needed nodes and scalar edge properties, avoiding unused nullable edges.
Preserve relationship-bag multiplicity, NULLs and zero-neighbor groups.
For three-valued WHERE negation, guard compared operands IS NOT NULL before NOT.
When counting entities, count the actual declared non-null primary property;
do not use a node-object COUNT DISTINCT that can bypass an expansion here.
Native datetime literals use a space separator and up to six fractional digits.
Do not guess timezones or silently drop precision. BOOL values are true/false.
No writes/admin/procedures. Return only requested scalar/list/map properties,
not node/relationship/path objects. No default LIMIT; preserve requested order.

Otherwise return {"status":"ANSWER","calls":[selection],"combine":{"op":"single"}}.
A selection has nodes:[{id,label}], edges:[{id,source,target,label,optional?}],
where:[{field,op,value?|other_field?,negate?}], returns:[{field,alias,agg?,distinct?}].
Use actual schema labels/properties and directed endpoints. Field is a variable
plus actual property, e.g. p.<actual primary property>, never a fabricated eid.
Up to four connected nodes and three edges; the first node is the required root.
Mandatory edges share one MATCH, with distinct relationship bindings. At most
one optional edge can attach to required endpoints and introduce a nullable node.
Global where filters apply after optional expansion. Count nullable primary
properties/nodes for zero groups; count(*) also counts the unmatched root row.
where is a conjunction, with eq,ne,lt,le,gt,ge,in,contains,starts_with,ends_with,
is_null,not_null. negate applies three-valued NOT; other_field compares same types.
BOOL admits eq/ne/in/null checks. DATE uses ISO dates. DATETIME admits scalar
comparisons of naive ISO timestamps at microsecond precision; no timezone guess.
returns aggregates: count,sum,avg,min,max,collect; count also admits * or a node variable.
Optional group_by lists actual property keys; to keep same-named entities apart,
group by the declared primary property. Other selection fields: distinct,
order_by:[{column,direction:"ASC"|"DESC"}], limit only when the question requests it.
For union/intersection/difference use exactly two unaggregated/unordered/unlimited
selections, with aligned columns, projecting the answer entity's primary as id.
All payload must belong to that same entity type. combine is {op,key:"id",
output:"count",alias}, or output:"rows",columns:[requested aliases].
No arbitrary query/expression text, subqueries, variable-length paths, multiple
optional edges, HAVING, regex, arithmetic or multi-stage summary joins.
Do not discard an unsupported condition or silently fall back to direct Cypher.
